questions.question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Students in class B are much quiet than students in class C.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the use of the adjective "**quiet**" instead of the comparative adjective "**quieter**."
 
• Comparative adjectives are used to compare differences between the two objects they modify (in this case, students in class B and students in class C).
 
• The correct phrase should be "**much quieter than**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 2** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *Students in class B are much quieter than students in class C.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part 1: "Students in class B are,"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Part 3: "students in class C."** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **No error** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part 2.

questions.question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select No error’,

Never put of / until tomorrow what / you can do today.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 3' i.e. '**Never put of'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the phrasal verb **"put of".**
 
• The correct phrasal verb should be** "put off" **which means to delay or postpone.
 
• The segment **"Never put of"** should be corrected to **"Never put off".**
 
• Using **"of"** instead of **"off"** alters the intended meaning of the phrase.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *'Never put off until tomorrow what you can do today'.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"You can do today"** and **"until tomorrow what"** are correct in the context of the sentence.
 
• **"Off" **(बंद) in this context is a preposition indicating a change in position or state, while** "of" **(का) indicates belonging or association.

Although people had been on watch and / the watchkeepers were very, very tired, / everyone were up and buzzing.

options.text: Although people had been on watch and
the watchkeepers were very, very tired,

questions.solution:
Here, the erroneous part is **"everyone were up and buzzing."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The subject **"everyone"** is singular, but the verb **"were"** is incorrect as it is the past tense of **"be"** and should be replaced with** "was" **to agree with the singular** "everyone."**
 
• **“Everyone”** is treated as singular pronoun, so it's always used with a singular verb form.
 
 
• **Example: *****Everyone is**__ responsible for this failure.*
 
 
 
• The correct sentence would be *"Although people had been on watch and the watchkeepers were very, very tired, __**everyone was up and buzzing**__."*
 
• The correct answer is Option 1.

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

The little boy complained me about his careless nanny.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'complained me'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **'Complain'** is a verb which means **"​to say that you are annoyed, unhappy or not satisfied about somebody/something".**

 
 
• **E.g**. Poor residents complained to the police.
 
 
 
• 'Complain' is followed by the preposition** 'to'**, when the person to whom you are complaining is mentioned.
 
 
• **E.g.** I **complained to** the customer service representative.
 
 
 
• According to the rule and example that are given above,** 'complained to me'** will be used instead of** 'complained me'.**

 

**Correct Sentence:** *The little boy **complained to me **about his careless nanny.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Difference between complain and complaint-**

 
 
• **'Complain'** is a **verb*** *which means "​to say that you are annoyed, unhappy or not satisfied about somebody/something".

 
 
• **E.g.** Tourists **complained** about the lack of toilet facilities in the area.
 
 
 
• **'Complaint'** is a **noun** which means "a statement that somebody makes saying that they are not satisfied".
 
 
• **E.g.** The most common **complaint **is about poor service.

questions.solution:

• **The verb tense in this part of the sentence is incorrect. **
 
• **"Were" is in the past tense, while "will" is in the future tense.**
 
• The sentence is referring to a situation in future. 
 
• Thus, to maintain proper tense agreement, the correct version of this sentence would be:
 
 
• "If things are not going to be normal after the pandemic, mankind will have to accept the New Normal."
 
 

Thus, **the correct answer is option 3**.

Platinum is costlier than any other metals found on earth.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 3.

In the given sentence, 'costlier' is in comparative degree but the comparative degree is used only when we are comparing between two objects.
